messages:
alex: noticing elevated provisioning failures in eu-central-2 for GPU pools, spike starting ~10:12 UTC :warning:
maya: saw it too, autoscaler pods are flapping, some nodes not joining cluster
liam: getting `JoinTimeout` on the node bootstrap logs, looks like cloud-provider API rate limit errors
sre-oncall: confirmed, control plane reports quota-throttling on instance create calls, affecting all p3/p4 SKUs in eu-central-2
cloud-ops: raising a support ticket with provider now, asking for quota bump and investigation (ref INC-12481)
emily: customer impact? which customers are hitting failures?
support-lead: Support queue already receiving 3 high-priority cases (enterprise customers with Dedicated pools). Notified AMs.
alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaler for affected nodegroups, 2) shift new allocation traffic to eu-west-1 and us-west-2 via routing policy, 3) enable fallback to smaller-quantized model variants for best-effort workloads
maya: commands to scale down autoscaler: `kubectl -n infra scale deploy/gpu-autoscaler --replicas=0` -- do we want to pause or scale to 1?
sre-oncall: pause (replicas=0) to stop noisy creates while provider sorts quota. run `kubectl apply -f /runbooks/autoscaler-pause.yaml`
liam: preparing traffic-shift playbook. Will update LB rules and routing weights: set eu-central-2 weight 0.2 for critical customers, 0 for best-effort.
emily: drafting status page text: 
statuspage-bot: DRAFT STATUS PAGE: 
- Component: eu-central-2 GPU provisioning
- Impact: New GPU node provisioning failures may prevent reservations and autoscaling for hosted and dedicated workloads. Ongoing requests may experience provisioning delays or fallbacks.
- Current status: Investigating
- Next update: in 15 minutes

support-lead: suggested ETA for next stable state? If provider restores quota, expect provisioning to resume within 45-90 minutes; cross-region shift should reduce customer failures in ~10-20 minutes once routing updates propagate.
cloud-ops: provider acknowledged quota throttle and says they are expediting. They've raised internal DC rate limits; waiting confirmation.
alex: please include callouts about potential additional egress costs for customers shifted cross-region. Support team prep a billing note for AMs.
support-lead: noted. drafting customer comms snippet with cost warning: 
> We're routing allocation requests to alternate regions which may incur cross-region egress charges. We'll provide detailed billing guidance after the incident. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
liam: executing weighted routing change now (`infra-router set-weight eu-central-2 0.2 --dry-run` then apply). Will post when live.
maya: also seeing some KV cache mismatch errors after partial failovers; may need to invalidate certain caches to avoid serving stale completions.
sre-oncall: run `redis-cli -h cache-eu-central-2 --scan | xargs -n 100 redis-cli -h cache-eu-central-2 del` only after shift completes. We'll coordinate.
alex: support-lead, please proactively reach out to the 3 impacted enterprise customers with the ETA and mention dedicated fallback options (reserved pools in other regions or temporarily increasing burst capacity).
support-lead: on it. I'll ping AMs and create 1:1 escalation threads.
statuspage-bot: Published: eu-central-2 GPU provisioning — Investigating. Next update at +15m.
emily: published the short status and included the ETA window 45-90m. Added link to support contact channel.
cloud-ops: provider just replied: "Temporary quota window opened, but we recommend throttled rollout to avoid further API rate limits." They set soft limit to 60 ops/min for our account.
liam: we'll do a controlled rollout: 5 nodes every 2 minutes to avoid hitting 60 ops/min. Starting now.
maya: first batch shows nodes successfully joining. Monitoring cluster health: `k get nodes | grep gpu | tail -n 10`
sre-oncall: monitoring CPU/memory of autoscaler and gating controllers. If we see repeated failures, we'll revert to manual provisioning and keep autoscaler paused.
emily: support-lead shared the customer note drafts, asking for approval: short, transparent, mention ETA, workaround, potential cost, and follow-up charge reconciliation.
support-lead: approved. Sending to top-3 affected customers now. Templates in `docs/incidents/`
alex: once provider finishes, we need a postmortem with timeline, root cause (quota/rate-limit), and an action list: pre-approve higher burst, add graceful backoff in autoscaler, add provider-side request pacing.
sre-oncall: opening postmortem ticket INC-12481-PM and assigning owners.
cloud-ops: provider confirms we've been removed from throttle at 10:58 UTC. Continuing to observe for 30m before full routing normalization.
liam: beginning normalization: increase eu-central-2 weight back to 0.8 over 10 minutes.
statuspage-bot: Update: eu-central-2 GPU provisioning — Partial Recovery. New provisioning resuming with rate limits in place. Next update in 30m.
support-lead: all affected customers acknowledged; one requested invoice reconciliation for egress — flagged for billing ops.
emily: drafting post-incident status page summary and comms for tomorrow.
alex: good work. takeaways for immediate action: (1) add provider API rate limit alerts (2) implement autoscaler backoff + jitter (3) playbook for cross-region routing with billing notification toggles.
maya: adding items to infra backlog. :thumbsup:
liam: closing the coordination loop, will monitor until last_message_ts.
sre-oncall: incident marked as mitigated, but will remain open for postmortem and follow-ups.
statuspage-bot: Final update planned in 3 hours with postmortem link."
